  1. Play with a band
  2. Sequencers & Arpeggiators

Sequencers & Arpeggiators

Every kind of sequencer and arpeggiator as a small working instrument on one clock: arpeggiators, step and x0x grids, acid bass, analog knobs, conditional trigs, Euclidean, polymetric, Cartesian, Turing Machine, Markov, Game of Life, piano roll, tracker and loop recording. Play any two side by side.

Every sequencer answers the same two questions in its own way: which note next and when. This page has one of each main kind, all running on the same clock, so you can hear them against each other. Hold a chord below, then press ▶ on any card, or run two at once in Compare two. The cards that read the held chord are the arpeggiators and a few sequencers that follow the chords; the rest use the key and scale.

Input and tempo

Compare two

Pick any two kinds. They start together on the next beat, A in the left ear and B in the right, with their own controls.

Arpeggiators

An arpeggiator needs a chord held down: it decides the order and the rate, you decide the notes.

Step sequencers

You write each step by hand. The pattern loops exactly, except where a step carries a rule.

Pattern math

The pattern comes from a rule or a shape: spread hits evenly, let tracks of different lengths drift, walk a grid.

Generative

You set the odds; the machine picks the notes. Good for music that keeps changing without anyone touching it.

Linear and recorded

No looping grid as the starting point: notes laid out in time, typed in rows, or played in and kept.

Side-by-side table

Click a heading to sort, a family to filter, a name to jump to its card.

Works Cited

“Arp Settings Basics.” Yamaha Synth Forum, Montage series. yamahasynth.com/community/montage-series-synthesizers/arp-settings-basics. Forum answer by Bad Mister: the five key modes, and Velocity Mode Original (as recorded) or Thru (your velocity influences each note).

Bad Mister. “Arpeggiator Key Modes.” Yamaha Synth, Yamaha Corporation of America. yamahasynth.com/learn/moxf-series-music-production-synthesizers/arpeggiator-key-modes-moxf/. Written for the MOXF; the source for what Sort, Thru, Direct, Sort+Direct and Thru+Direct sound, and velocity limits splitting one arp across parts.
